1c11me2:188: Traditional LLM evaluation often only looks at the quality of the final output while ignoring the intermediate process. Many meaningful behaviors of an Agent—the choice of tool calls, the reasonableness of decision paths, the way errors are handled—are only exposed during real execution. This means that if you only evaluate the output results, you will miss a large amount of important information about Agent capabilities. Trajectory eval records the complete message sequence, tool calls, and decision points, allowing evaluators to trace back and review the entire execution process, not just the final answer.

1xk40li:196: The four matching modes (strict/unordered/subset/superset) reflect different definitions of "correctness" in different scenarios. Strict mode suits compliance scenarios with clear standard operating procedures; unordered suits cases where step order does not matter; subset allows flexible omission of optional steps; superset allows additional defensive behaviors. Understanding this trade-off is important: being too strict will reject correct executions due to insignificant differences, while being too lenient may let real errors pass.
